title: Playing silent pictures at the Criterion Theater from cue sheets
summary: Taking over Shirley Clay's theater job, he read overtures and Sam Fox folio music matched to film cue sheets.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Singleton, he was something! Well, then I played around and giged around there for awhile and then after I ran into this fellow -- dead now, Shirley Clay, he asked me if I wanted his permanent job. I told him yes. He said, 'Well, I'm going to New York,' he says, 'and you can have this job playing the theater,' -- the Cranshaw -- at the Hip -- no, at the Criterion Theater, just playing pictures, you know. Of course, you had toplay good music.
When silent movies came along, you know, came into town, did sheet music accompany them, you know, did you have certain music that you had to use?
Yeah, that's right, you had a score -- they would send you a cue sheet and you'd have to go buy or go

to the library. And at that time Sam Fox -- Sam Fox Folios -- you would have -- they had that music to offer -- you know, they know all about that I guess -- what kind of music to have in a library for pictures. And you could get that -- you get the number that they wanted or a facsimile thereof, you know.
And you'd get a chance to play -- well, we had to play all of the standard overtures and selections and things like that.
All these jobs were reading jobs in theaters, of course. (unintelligible)

Oh, yes, they were reading -- and you would get -- that's where you really get a kick because you play some pretty music. I never will forget the number where we would have Oriental pictures like something like the Japanese or something like that -- we would play "Japanese Sunset," and that was really pretty, really something. Come out of the (unintelligible) Sam Fox Folios, see.
